precepts.text: So out of the abundance of your heart, your mouth speaketh.
precepts.point: So the sixth place is understanding. And in the seventh, speech. The seventh is speech. The speech is the interpretation of what your mind meditates on. So out of the abundance of your heart, your mouth speaketh. These are the senses. Now read the next one. Verse six.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
Sirach names the senses the Most High gave man: “They received the use of the five operations of the Lord, and in the sixth place he imparted them understanding, and in the seventh speech, an interpreter of the cogitations thereof.” Cogitation is the act of thinking very carefully and deeply about a subject, or a carefully considered thought itself; meditation is a good word for it too, the capacity to think or reflect.

So the sixth is understanding and the seventh is speech, and speech is the interpretation of what your mind meditates on. That is why “out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.” What you meditate on is what comes out of your mouth.

Thinking and reflecting do not work unless they are funnelled through the word of God; that is how your mind has to work. If you are not moving right, the thought that comes out is going to be off, and so will the speech that interprets it.

The list goes on: “Counsel, and a tongue, and eyes, ears, and a heart, gave he them to understand. Withal he filled them with the knowledge of understanding, and shewed them good and evil.” The tongue is the instrument we use to form our words. Counsel is a man weighing options and determining what should be done, but he must be a godly man who surrounds himself with godly people. A mind fed on porn and then making decisions will make a mistake, and a mouth speaking out of that heart will show it. These senses are given so we can understand good and evil, and they have to be exercised in the word.

precepts.text: O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? For out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh. Christ called them vipers; John called them vipers; the same serpents Isaiah 59 describes.
precepts.point: The way of peace they know not; and there is no judgment in their goings: they have made them crooked paths; whosoever goeth therein shall not know peace. You follow the Democratic or the Republican party, you follow the cross and the idols, you are not going to find peace. Our people have made crooked paths for themselves.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
Now Christ is speaking to them: “O generation of vipers”. That goes back to Isaiah 59, the cockatrice' eggs that break out into a viper. Christ called them vipers, and John the Baptist called them vipers. And their children are little snakes too.

“how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.” What is in the heart comes out of the mouth. A generation of vipers cannot speak good things, because what fills their heart is evil.

That is Isaiah 59 again. Before verse 5, verse 3 said our lips have spoken lies and our tongue perverseness. The lips speak lies and the tongue perverseness because the heart is full of iniquity, and the eggs they hatch are the same kind as the ones who laid them.

precepts.text: And whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but unto him that blasphemeth against the Holy Ghost it shall not be forgiven.
precepts.point: And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

precepts.why:
Luke gives the same word Christ spoke in Matthew 12: “And whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but unto him that blasphemeth against the Holy Ghost it shall not be forgiven.” It shall not be forgiven. A word against Christ himself can be forgiven; a word against the Holy Ghost, the power of Christ, what he was doing, cannot.

Why did he say it? Because of what they said earlier in the chapter: he casteth out devils by devils. Christ answered, No, I by the Spirit of God cast out devils, and if I do that, the kingdom is here with you, meaning himself. Christ was healing the people with the Spirit of God, and they said the spirit he was using to heal was the devil. They were speaking evil of his power. That is blaspheming the Holy Spirit itself.

Mark, Peter's scribe, gives the same account in more detail. “He hath Beelzebub, and by the prince of the devils casteth he out devils.” Christ asked them, “How can Satan cast out Satan?” Why would Satan cast himself out? That makes no sense. “And if a kingdom be divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand”; that is why we fell. “And if Satan rise up against himself, and be divided, he cannot stand, but hath an end.” That is happening right now, America and Israel turning against each other, America burning bridges and going against NATO. Esau has an end.

Then Mark makes it plain: “he that shall blaspheme against the Holy Ghost hath never forgiveness, but is in danger of eternal damnation: Because they said, He hath an unclean spirit.” Ghost, spirit: same thing, don't let the words fool you. That's the difference. They said the power Christ used to heal the people did not come from God but from the devil, and if they kept that mindset to death, that was it for them.

Brought to now: those who were once enlightened, who “were made partakers of the Holy Ghost”, and then fall away and call this truth a cult, blaspheme that same Spirit. Die in that without repenting and you're finished, a dead man or a dead woman walking.

precepts.text: A good man out of the good treasure of the heart bringeth forth good things; every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment; by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words condemned. If you cannot prove it in the scriptures, it is an idle word. These men condemn themselves trying to sound deep when the Lord said his laws are simple.
precepts.point: Because judgment is not executed speedily they think they can say anything about Jesus; he is writing it in a book and coming back to say, say that to my face. That is how you know Jesus is a black man.

note.label: Fixx Ya Face Fridays | as Was Supposed!!

precepts.why:
Enoch prophesied “Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, To execute judgment upon all”, and to convince the ungodly “of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.” Off top, he rides deep; he's got a crew. Because judgment is not executed speedily, they think they can say whatever they want about Jesus: a stripper, making it rain on him. He's getting it all written down in a book, and he's coming back to say, say that to my face. That's how you know Jesus is a black man.

Christ said it himself: “A good man out of the good treasure of the heart bringeth forth good things: and an evil man out of the evil treasure bringeth forth evil things.” That is what comes out of you. “But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.” If you cannot prove it in the scriptures, it is an idle word. “For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.”

These men are condemning themselves. It isn't enough to say Jesus is my way because he gave his life for us; he has to be a stripper, butt naked. They sit down and write these sermons thinking they are saying something deep and profound. Why go through all that to concoct lies when the Lord said his laws are simple? There is simplicity in Christ, and keeping God's commandments is very easy to do. Every idle word will be accounted for in that day.

precepts.text: Every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment. Idle means idolatrous; the Most High records everything.
precepts.point: Rabshakeh had cried in the Jews' language: let not Hezekiah make you trust in the Lord; make an agreement with me by a present and I will carry you to a land like your own; which of the gods of the nations delivered his land out of my hand? The people held their peace at the king's commandment.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.why:
The Lord asks Sennacherib, “Whom hast thou reproached and blasphemed? and against whom hast thou exalted thy voice, and lifted up thine eyes on high? even against the Holy One of Israel.” By his messengers he had reproached the Lord with his boasting words, and every one of them came up into the Lord's ears: “thy rage against me and thy tumult is come up into mine ears”. The same words also remind our people how we have despised the Lord.

Christ said, “every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.” We have to be mindful of this. Sometimes we speak frivolous things and don't realize the Most High is recording everything. Idle means idolatrous: every idolatrous word we speak.

Sennacherib's words were recorded and answered: the Lord put his hook in his nose and turned him back the way he came. So be careful what comes out of your mouth; the Most High hears it all and will bring it to account.

precepts.text: Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation.
precepts.point: We have given the hand to the Egyptians to be satisfied with bread, and watched for a nation that could not save us.

note.label: Christ: the Enemy of Christianity

precepts.why:
America knows terrorists are in this country, yet it is looking at the wrong immigrants: the Mexicans, our people from Venezuela, from Haiti, from Jamaica. Those are the aliens they chase, when the real aliens are the ones who took our inheritance. And it is causing a divide in Babylon the Great. Christ said: “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation”.

That started with us. When the 12 tribes split, after that split we fell, and the 12 tribes were brought to desolation, with 70 AD soon approaching. But the statement Christ made wasn't just for us. It applied to Rome, which was dominant over us at that time, and to the European nations and countries as well.

“and every city or house divided against itself shall not stand”. You could go deep with that in the house too, husbands and wives divided against each other: if your family is divided, your house is going to fall.

The prophecy shows it coming on spiritual Egypt, Babylon the Great: “And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother, and every one against his neighbour”. I will set the Americans against the Americans. That is a house divided, internal warfare, and there will be a civil war in this country. So the nation we watched to save us is a divided house that cannot stand, and we must not look to it for our help.

precepts.text: Christ said, If I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your children cast them out? He mentioned the name of another god and did no sin.
precepts.point: Joshua and Deuteronomy double it: neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow yourselves unto them; and if thy brother or son or wife entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, thou shalt not consent. Wherever you are, do not go trying to find out how the nations worship their gods.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

precepts.why:
To “make no mention of the name of other gods” is not saying you cannot pronounce the names Buddha, Allah, Krishna, Ra. Christ himself said, “And if I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your children cast them out? therefore they shall be your judges.” Beelzebub is the chief of the devils, a name derived from the Philistine god of Ekron. Christ named him, and Christ did no sin; so the verse cannot mean the bare saying of a name.

The Lord says this same thing three ways in this one chapter, and the other two places show the meaning: in verse 24, thou shalt not bow down to their gods nor serve them nor do after their works; and in verses 32 and 33, thou shalt make no covenant with them nor with their gods, for if thou serve their gods it will surely be a snare unto thee. Make no mention means do not learn how to serve and worship them.

precepts.text: A man is better than a sheep lifted out of the pit on the sabbath; wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.
precepts.point: The Lord gives no man license to sin, but Christ is Lord of the sabbath and brought grace for necessities out of our control, a blown tire or an empty tank on the way to keep the sabbath, or medicine when the body is in danger; it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.

note.label: Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign

precepts.why:
“What man shall there be among you, that shall have one sheep, and if it fall into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not lay hold on it, and lift it out? How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.”

The Lord gives no man license to sin, but Christ brought grace for necessities out of our control: a blown tire or an empty tank on the way to keep the sabbath, or medicine when the body is in danger. A man is better than a sheep lifted out of the pit; it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.

precepts.text: The Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day; grace covers what is out of our control, never license to sin.
precepts.point: The Lord gives no man license to sin, but Christ is Lord of the sabbath and brought grace for necessities out of our control, a blown tire or an empty tank on the way to keep the sabbath, or medicine when the body is in danger; it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.

note.label: Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign

precepts.why:
“For the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day.” Christ is Lord of the sabbath, and he brought grace for necessities out of our control, a blown tire or an empty tank on the way to keep the sabbath, or medicine when the body is in danger.

That grace is never license to sin. “every one that defileth it shall surely be put to death”: the stoning was done away in Christ, but the judgment for breaking the sabbath still stands, and people still die on the sabbath day, Friday sundown to Saturday sundown. The Most High is justified, because it is his sign between him and his people.

precepts.text: On the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath and are blameless; if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.
precepts.point: Jeremiah carries the same word: I spake not unto your fathers concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices, but this thing commanded I them, obey my voice. Yet they hearkened not, but walked in the counsels of their evil heart and went backward and not forward; speak all these words unto them, but they will not hearken. That is seen every sabbath on the streets.

note.label: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out

precepts.why:
Christ used this very law on the Pharisees: “have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless?” The priests had fire going in the temple every sabbath by commandment, and they were blameless.

“But I say unto you, That in this place is one greater than the temple. But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.” Israel leaned so heavily on the sacrifices instead of applying the commandments that they were confounded and could not see Christ as the Son of God when he came.

precepts.text: The priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless; the sabbath offerings were commanded work.
precepts.point: This is also why Christ had to come. In captivity we have no lambs, no farms, no temple, no most holy place, no veil, no high priest; the handwriting of ordinances that was against us was taken out of the way and nailed to his cross. Those who deny Christ and claim the Old Testament only are not keeping these sacrifices, and without Christ the whole law, drink offering to meat offering, still stands over them.

note.label: Numbers 28: The Continual Burnt Offering and the Offerings of the Feasts

precepts.why:
On the sabbath day two more lambs were offered with their meat and drink offerings, “the burnt offering of every sabbath, beside the continual burnt offering”: four lambs every sabbath, with the drink offerings attached. Precept upon precept this answers what Christ told the Pharisees.

“Or have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless?” Israel did not kindle fire for themselves on the sabbath, but this altar work was the ordinance of the Lord for every sabbath day. The priests were commanded to do it, so they were blameless.

precepts.text: All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men, but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven.
precepts.point: Swearing on the Bible in the court system is another matter: be subject unto the higher powers, for the powers that be are ordained of God, and you also have the option to affirm; either way, tell the truth.

note.label: Numbers 30: The Law of Vows

precepts.why:
If you vowed ignorantly and could not fulfill it, there is forgiveness: “Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven unto men.”

“And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.” The only thing not forgiven is blasphemy against the Holy Ghost, which is speaking evil of this truth after receiving it. A vow broken in ignorance is not that.

precepts.text: But do not ask for signs like that anymore; an evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign. He gave us all the signs back in the day, he split the Red Sea and we still became rebellious, so the walk we are in now is by faith.
precepts.point: Gideon asks the fleece signs: dew on the fleece only with dry earth beside, and then the reverse, dew on all the ground with the fleece dry. The Lord commands the dew, the condensation that falls through the night, to land exactly where he pleases; God can do whatever he wants, infinite power.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
But do not ask for signs like Gideon's fleece anymore. Christ answered, “An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas.”

He gave us all the signs back in the day. He split the Red Sea, and we still became rebellious. So the walk we are in now is by faith, not by laying out a fleece and waiting on the dew.

precepts.text: Every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment; by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned. Make sure what comes out of your mouth is calculated; that whole "we were arguing and it just slipped" will not fly on judgment day. Repent, and make a door and a bar for thy mouth, as the scriptures say.
precepts.point: All of us in this walk, keeping the commandments and the faith in Christ, have taken covenant and proclaimed out of our mouths that we are going to endure to the end; we broke the bread and drank the wine and took the covenant with the Lord. Now the Lord is judging you by your actions: are you going to endure to the end, whether to Christ's return or until you leave this earth, if you truly love him?

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
“That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment. For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.”

“Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth.” Make sure what comes out of your mouth is calculated. That whole, we were arguing and it just slipped, will not fly on judgment day. Repent, and make a door and a bar for thy mouth, as the scriptures say.

precepts.text: Have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless? In this place is one greater than the temple; and if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.
precepts.point: Christ spoke about that fire in the temple: on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless. Israel was not to kindle a fire on the sabbath when it comes to food, but the priests had to keep that fire burning, and they sacrificed on the sabbath days, a lamb in the morning and a lamb in the evening; they broke the sabbath yet are blameless, because they were doing thus saith the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
Christ spoke about that fire in the temple: “Or have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless?” Israel was not to kindle a fire on the sabbath when it comes to food, but the priests had to keep that fire burning. They broke the sabbath, yet are blameless, because they were doing thus saith the Lord.

“But I say unto you, That in this place is one greater than the temple. But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.” Sacrifice was never the most important thing to the Lord: not the blood of bulls and of goats, but mercy upon one another and the keeping of the commandments.

precepts.text: If the Most High cast out devils by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God is come unto you.
precepts.point: But Christ told us if we keep the commandments and follow him, we will rule on thrones with him, so there is falsehood in Eliphaz's answer.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
“But if I cast out devils by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God is come unto you.” If the Most High cast out devils by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God is come unto you. That kingdom is the answer to Eliphaz. He asks, “Is it any pleasure to the Almighty, that thou art righteous? or is it gain to him, that thou makest thy ways perfect?”, throwing Job's righteousness back as filthy rags, as if keeping the commandments profits nothing.

But there is a kingdom of God that comes, and Christ told us if we keep the commandments and follow him, we will rule on thrones with him. So there is falsehood in Eliphaz's answer.

precepts.text: We are judged by our words, for the Most High hears all our words and even our thoughts, so nothing can be withholden from Him.
precepts.point: Dust and ashes refer to the custom our forefathers had of putting ashes on the head as a sign of sorrow and repentance.

note.label: Job 42: The Lord Turned the Captivity of Job

precepts.why:
Job confesses, “I know that thou canst do every thing, and that no thought can be withholden from thee.” This is a little thing in the scriptures to take heed to. Christ says, “For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.”

We are judged by our words, and the Most High hears all our words and even our thoughts, so nothing can be withholden from him. The hatred or the private spirit a man carries cannot be hidden from him; he knows the inward parts of men. Job had heard of him by the hearing of the ear, but now his eye sees him, and so he abhors himself and repents in dust and ashes, the custom our forefathers had of putting ashes on the head as a sign of sorrow and repentance.

precepts.text: Whosoever does the will of the Father is His brother, sister, and mother, above the ties of one's own people.
precepts.point: This is the woman leaving her father's house for her husband's house when we live righteously; she now cares to please her husband.

note.label: Psalm 45: Thy Throne, O God, Is Forever

precepts.why:
“forget also thine own people, and thy father’s house”. Christ showed what stands above the ties of one's own people. When told “thy mother and thy brethren stand without, desiring to speak with thee”, he answered, “Who is my mother? and who are my brethren?” and stretched forth his hand toward his disciples: “Behold my mother and my brethren! For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.”

Whosoever does the will of the Father is his brother, sister and mother, above one's own people and father's house. So the daughter who hearkens, forgets her own people and worships her Lord is doing the will of the Father, and the king greatly desires her beauty.

precepts.text: Christ's warning that men give account of every idle word, matching Solomon's charge to let your words be few.
precepts.point: Be not rash with your mouth nor let your heart be hasty to utter anything before the Most High, for he is in heaven and you upon earth; therefore let your words be few. This means watch your mouth, which is why Christ said you will give account of every word.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 5: Vows, Riches, and the Gift of God

precepts.why:
“But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.”

Solomon says “Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter any thing before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.” This means watch your mouth, which is why Christ said you will give account of every word. Every idle word is accounted for in the day of judgment, so let your words be few, and be more ready to hear than to give the sacrifice of fools, for “a fool’s voice is known by multitude of words.”

precepts.text: If we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins.
precepts.point: The distinction is between what falls out and what is planned. A sheep does not fall into a pit by appointment, and spilt milk is cleaned up when it happens. Wilful sin is the thing thought out beforehand.

note.label: Matthew 12: Lord of the Sabbath and the Blasphemy Against the Holy Ghost

precepts.why:
They set a man with a withered hand before him and asked, “Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath days? that they might accuse him.” His answer: a man with one sheep that falls into a pit on the sabbath day, “will he not lay hold on it, and lift it out? How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.”

The distinction is between what falls out and what is planned. A sheep does not fall into a pit by appointment, and spilt milk is cleaned up when it happens. What is condemned is the wilful thing, the thing thought out beforehand: “For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins”. Wilful sin, after the knowledge of the truth has been received, is the sin with no more sacrifice for it.

Lifting a sheep out of a pit, or healing a man whose hand was withered, is doing well when the need falls out on the sabbath; it is not a wilful breaking of it, and it is lawful.

precepts.text: The prophecy quoted: mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth; a bruised reed shall he not break.
precepts.point: This too was written beforehand: behold my servant, whom I have chosen, and he shall shew judgment to the Gentiles.

note.label: Matthew 12: Lord of the Sabbath and the Blasphemy Against the Holy Ghost

precepts.why:
The Pharisees held a council how they might destroy him, and he withdrew, healed the multitudes that followed, and “charged them that they should not make him known”. This too was written beforehand, and Matthew says so: “That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet”.

Isaiah: “Behold my servant, whom I uphold; mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth; I have put my spirit upon him: he shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles.” The servant, the elect in whom the Lord's soul delights, with the spirit put upon him, is Christ, and he shall shew judgment to the Gentiles.

“He shall not cry, nor lift up, nor cause his voice to be heard in the street.” That is why he withdrew from the council and charged the people not to make him known: no crying in the streets. “A bruised reed shall he not break, and the smoking flax shall he not quench: he shall bring forth judgment unto truth.” The one the Pharisees wanted to destroy was quietly healing them all, breaking no bruised reed and quenching no smoking flax, exactly as it was written.

note.label: Matthew 12: Lord of the Sabbath and the Blasphemy Against the Holy Ghost

precepts.why:
“All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven unto men.” Not in this world, nor in the world to come.

The Holy Ghost is bound to the law, so speaking against it is not only with the mouth. Hebrews describes the man who does it: “For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.”

These were enlightened; they tasted the heavenly gift and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost. Then they fell away. Going back into the world and back into the ways that were left is a man's actions speaking for him, and that is speaking against the Holy Ghost he partook of. For such a one it is impossible to be renewed again unto repentance; he crucifies the Son of God afresh, and there is no forgiveness for it. That is the blasphemy that is not forgiven.

note.label: John 2: The First Miracle and the Cleansing of the Temple

precepts.why:
The scribes and Pharisees asked the same thing: “Master, we would see a sign from thee.” Christ answered, “An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas: For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.”

That is the same sign given in other words. In John 2 he said, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” In Matthew, as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly, so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth. Both are the sign of his death and his rising the third day, the one sign that generation would be given.

And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.”

The blasphemy against the Holy Ghost is subverting the doctrine, speaking heresies, bringing blasphemous doctrines, going against the laws of God. That is why the one who preaches another gospel is accursed: it is not forgiven in this world nor in the world to come.
